basis: Ancestors and phenotypes identify a limb reduction syndrome: split hands, short tibiae and finger contractures; no established extra-skeletal damage.
Severe developmental impairment, microcephaly, joint contractures and foot deformities define the syndrome; cardiac and pulmonary malformations occur in <30%.
Myocardial noncompaction causes ventricular dysfunction and conduction abnormalities; extra-cardiac embolic injury is a minority complication.
Bacterial infection of the vagina supports the infection mechanism axis; the reproductive site has no anatomical axis.
Inherited retinal degeneration caused by biallelic ABCA4 variants; no established systemic organ involvement.
Cobalamin disorder with anemia/neutropenia; developmental delay 2/2 and cardiac defects/pulmonary hypertension 1/2. Skeletal maturation abnormalities 1/2 omitted by cap; cohort very small.
Palmoplantar/periorificial keratoderma, abnormal nails and corneal epithelial dysplasia define the syndrome.
CACNA1D neurodevelopmental disorder with aldosteronism; ventricular hypertrophy 80-99%, conduction disease 30-79%. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; stones are separate.
Congenital inward turning of the eyelid is an ocular structural disorder.
Vertebral fusions, scoliosis and flexion contractures occur in 10/10; pterygia accompany the locomotor malformations. Cleft palate occurs in only 1/10.
Localized cutaneous mucinosis combining skin subtypes; systemic scleromyxedema involvement should not be extrapolated to this localized disease.
Carcinoma originates in cutaneous eccrine sweat glands; distant organ metastases are uncommon.
Umbrella for Flaviviridae infections; no single anatomical organ is directly damaged in most patients across the group.
Immune-mediated thyroid inflammation and fibrosis; vocal cord paralysis and tracheal stenosis occur in <30%; extracervical fibroinflammatory diseases are rare or separate.
Bilateral cortical malformation with seizures and developmental impairment; frequent esotropia does not establish direct ocular damage; hearing loss occurs in <30%.
Rickettsial infection directly causes pulmonary inflammation; no additional common organ damage is established for this concept.
Developmental communication disorder affecting speech function; no common direct damage to the mouth or larynx is established across this umbrella.
Hereditary cerebral small-vessel angiopathy directly affects brain vessels and cerebral white matter, causing ischemic neurological impairment.
Cobalamin remethylation defect with megaloblastic anemia; developmental impairment and brain injury 30-79% or higher. Eye findings nonspecific; blindness and thrombosis <30%.
Defective GH/IGF signaling defines this endocrine growth disorder; short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage; immune disease is subtype-specific.
Neuropathy, pituitary dysfunction and chorioretinal dystrophy define it. Renal insufficiency 30-79%; hearing loss 30-79% and frequent digital anomalies omitted by cap.
Inherited absence or deficiency of the plasma hemoglobin-scavenging protein haptoglobin; transfusion-related allergic reactions are not intrinsic organ involvement.
Neoplasm originates in cranial nerve tissue; additional organ dysfunction depends on the affected nerve and is not common across this umbrella.
Cutaneous lupus with characteristic erythema multiforme-like lesions; systemic lupus organ damage is not established as common across this syndrome.
Malignancy originates in peripheral or autonomic nervous tissue; anatomical sites and metastatic organ involvement vary across subtypes.
